What Are Options? Call and Put, Premium, Pay-offs and Pricing

An option gives the buyer the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell an asset at a set price by a set date. This guide covers calls and puts with worked pay-offs, how the premium is made up, and what moves it.

2 min readFor MBA, BBA and BBMUpdated 2 November 2026

Call and put options

PositionRight or dutyViewMaximum lossMaximum gain
Buy a callRight to buyPrice will risePremium paidUnlimited
Sell a callDuty to sellPrice won't riseUnlimitedPremium received
Buy a putRight to sellPrice will fallPremium paidStrike − premium (per share)
Sell a putDuty to buyPrice won't fallStrike − premium (per share)Premium received

Call option: worked example

Buy a call with a strike of ₹1,000 for a premium of ₹40, lot 500 (simplified). The cost is ₹20,000, and the break-even is 1,000 + 40 = ₹1,040.

Price at expiryValue per shareProfit per shareTotal profit or loss
₹950₹0−₹40−₹20,000
₹1,000₹0−₹40−₹20,000
₹1,040₹40₹0₹0
₹1,100₹100₹60+₹30,000

Put option: worked example

Buy a put with a strike of ₹1,000 for a premium of ₹35, lot 500. The break-even is 1,000 − 35 = ₹965.

Price at expiryValue per shareProfit per shareTotal profit or loss
₹1,050₹0−₹35−₹17,500
₹965₹35₹0₹0
₹900₹100₹65+₹32,500

Moneyness

StateCallPut
In the money (ITM)Price above strikePrice below strike
At the money (ATM)Price about equal to strikePrice about equal to strike
Out of the money (OTM)Price below strikePrice above strike

What the premium is made of

Premium = intrinsic value + time value. With the share at ₹1,050, a ₹1,000 call priced at ₹80 has an intrinsic value of ₹50 and a time value of ₹30.

Time value falls to zero at expiry, and this decay works against option buyers.

What moves the premium: the Greeks

GreekMeasures sensitivity to
DeltaA change in the underlying price
GammaHow fast delta itself changes
ThetaThe passage of time
VegaA change in implied volatility
RhoA change in interest rates

Pricing and parity

The Black-Scholes model values an option from five inputs: spot price, strike, time to expiry, interest rate and volatility. Of these, only volatility is unknown, which is why traders talk about implied volatility. Put-call parity links a call and a put with the same strike and expiry.

Put-call parity: call premium + present value of strike = put premium + spot price.

European and American

A European option can be exercised only at expiry, and an American option at any time before it. Index and stock options in India are European. Common strategies built from options include the protective put, covered call, straddle, strangle and spreads.

Exam and interview questions

What is the difference between a call and a put?

A call gives the right to buy at the strike price, and benefits from a rise. A put gives the right to sell at the strike price, and benefits from a fall.

Why does an option buyer pay a premium?

To get the right without the obligation. The seller takes on the obligation, and the risk, and is paid the premium for it.

What happens to an out-of-the-money option at expiry?

It expires worthless, and the buyer loses the whole premium.

Is option selling safer than buying?

It wins more often but carries a much larger potential loss, and needs a high margin. A seller of a naked call has theoretically unlimited risk.
